problem: Hire globally and run a company without offices.
title: GitLab operates as an all-remote, handbook-first company
context: GitLab says it became remote naturally as early team members chose to work from home.
decision_made: Stay fully remote with no company office, with a public handbook where every process change is documented first.
action_taken: Adopted written, asynchronous communication and a rule to move to a video call after three back-and-forth messages.
observed_outcome: Headcount grew to over 1,500 team members in more than 65 countries, and GitLab reports that 92 to 93 percent say it is a great place to work. Its CEO credits the all-remote policy for growth.
lessons: Remote work at scale needs heavy documentation and written-first habits.
limitations: Self-reported figures and survey results from different years. Growth attribution comes from the CEO. Start date is approximate. A reported $2.75 billion valuation was not confirmed.

claims.claim_text: GitLab operates all-remote with a handbook-first approach.
McKinsey's case study describes how GitLab thrives as an all-remote company.
